name: Stephen J. Squeri

career.title: Manager, Travelers Cheque Group; vice president from 1990
President, Establishment Services (U.S. & Canada), then President, Global Commercial Card
Executive Vice President and Chief Information Officer (also led Corporate Development)
Group President, Global Services, then Global Corporate Services

background_rationale: After four years as a consultant, he spent more than three decades inside American Express running merchant, commercial card, technology and corporate services businesses before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: American Express agreed to acquire restaurant-reservation platform Resy, an early step in building its dining benefits for card members.
American Express suspended its operations in Russia and Belarus following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
American Express agreed to pay about $230 million to resolve U.S. investigations into deceptive sales practices involving small-business card products.
American Express raised the U.S. Platinum Card annual fee to $895 from $695, its first increase since 2021, while adding new card benefits.

personal_story.hook: Stephen Squeri joined American Express as a manager in its traveler's cheque business in 1985 and became its CEO 33 years later.
personal_story.summary: Squeri, the grandchild of Italian and Irish immigrants, grew up in Astoria, Queens, where his father worked as an accountant for companies including Colgate, CBS and Bloomingdale's. At Monsignor McClancy High School he was in the National Honor Society and played on the basketball team, then followed his father to Manhattan College, studying accounting and computer science. After four years as a management consultant at Arthur Andersen, he joined American Express in 1985 as a manager in the Travelers Cheque Group. He worked his way through merchant services, commercial cards and the CIO job before succeeding Kenneth Chenault as chairman and CEO in February 2018.
